text: if you ask an engineer about how much time it'll cost to go and build something... it's almost always half the time as something that you are asking for, as a PM. And that motivation is so different.
speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
context: Lenny asks about how to balance letting engineers fix bugs they encounter versus maintaining team priorities and roadmaps. Yuhki explains the importance of bottom-up energy where developers notice problems and fix them organically. He shares insights about how engineer motivation dramatically affects project estimates and execution speed.
text_ko: 무언가를 만들어 달라고 엔지니어(engineer)에게 얼마나 걸리냐고 물어보면, 거의 항상 프로덕트 매니저(Product Manager)로서 당신이 요청한 시간의 절반 정도라고 얘기해요. 그리고 그 동기가 완전히 달라요.
text_zh: 你去问工程师把某个东西做出来要多久，他们给出的时间几乎总是只有你作为产品经理（PM）要求时间的一半。而且大家的出发点完全不一样。
text_es: Si le preguntas a un ingeniero cuánto tiempo le va a llevar construir algo, casi siempre te dirá que es la mitad de lo que tú, como responsable de producto (PM), pides. Y esa motivación es muy distinta.
original_text: And I think a lot of PMs have grown to realize this, which is, if you ask an engineer about how much time it'll cost to go and build something, and it's something that they came up with or they're advocating for, it's almost always half the time as something that you are asking for, as a PM. And that motivation is so different.

vocabulary.definition: The reason or reasons one has for acting or behaving in a particular way; the drive that compels individuals to pursue goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, motivation often refers to the factors that inspire employees to perform at their best, influencing productivity and engagement levels.
vocabulary.nuance: While motivation can be intrinsic or extrinsic, in a corporate setting, it often implies a need for external incentives or recognition.

text: I think one of the most powerful things, especially for startups, is that bottoms up energy, and maybe a developer noticing something is wrong and just going off and fixing it.
speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
context: Lenny discusses the tension between engineers wanting to fix bugs they encounter and product managers needing to maintain priorities. Yuhki advocates for allowing organic, bottom-up improvements rather than always enforcing top-down roadmap discipline, especially for startups where this grassroots energy can be more effective than formal quality metrics.
text_ko: 특히 스타트업에서는 보텀업 에너지(bottoms-up energy)가 정말 강력한 힘 중 하나라고 생각해요. 예를 들어 개발자가 뭔가 잘못된 걸 알아차리고 그냥 가서 바로 고쳐버리는 그런 거요.
text_zh: 我觉得，尤其对初创公司(startups)来说，最有力的就是那种自下而上的干劲(bottom-up energy)，比如开发者(developer)一发现哪儿不对，就直接去修。
text_es: Creo que una de las cosas más poderosas, especialmente para las empresas emergentes (startups), es esa energía que viene de abajo (bottoms up energy), y que un desarrollador (developer) se dé cuenta de que algo está mal y simplemente se ponga a arreglarlo.
key_sentence: one of the most powerful things, especially for startups, is that bottoms up energy
original_text: I think one of the most powerful things, especially for startups, is that bottoms up energy, and maybe a developer noticing something is wrong and just going off and fixing it. And for the most part, I try not to get in the way of that because if people are doing that constantly, and everyone the company is trying to make the product better, that is sometimes a way more effective way to improve the quality of experience than this top down of, oh, let's define this quality experience metric and try to change all the things, because you might miss these things.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity for vigorous activity; an exertion of physical or mental effort.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'energy' often refers to the enthusiasm and drive that employees bring to their work, which can significantly impact productivity and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: While it generally has a positive connotation, excessive energy can sometimes lead to burnout if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: The act of repairing or resolving an issue or problem.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, 'fixing' often refers to troubleshooting software bugs or operational inefficiencies, which is crucial for maintaining product quality and customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a reactive approach to problems, suggesting that issues are addressed only after they arise rather than being proactively prevented.

text: I think the most crazy version of it, maybe, is Dylan's always reading customer feedback. In fact, has reads the most customer feedback of all of us and has been doing that for a decade.
speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
context: Lenny asks what sets Figma apart in terms of customer proximity. Yuhki describes Figma's obsessive focus on customer feedback, explaining how CEO Dylan Field personally reads customer feedback daily and shares concerning tweets with the team. This level of founder involvement in customer feedback has been consistent for a decade.
text_ko: 아마 그 중 가장 극단적인 사례는 딜런이 항상 고객 피드백(customer feedback)을 읽고 있다는 거예요. 사실 우리 중에서 딜런이 가장 많은 고객 피드백을 읽고 있고, 그걸 10년째 해오고 있어요.
text_zh: 我觉得最夸张的例子可能就是Dylan总是在看客户反馈。实际上，他看客户反馈的量比我们任何人都多，而且已经坚持十年了。
text_es: Creo que la versión más loca de esto, quizá, es que Dylan está siempre leyendo los comentarios de los clientes (customer feedback). De hecho, lee más que cualquiera de nosotros y lleva haciéndolo una década.
key_sentence: Dylan reads the most customer feedback and shares concerning insights.
original_text: I think the most crazy version of it, maybe, is Dylan's always reading customer feedback. In fact, has reads the most customer feedback of all of us and has been doing that for a decade. And oftentimes, there used to be this thing where he would drop in tweets that he sees into different Slack channels to be like, hey, this seems concerning, or we're getting this feedback.

vocabulary.definition: Information and opinions provided by customers regarding their experiences with a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, customer feedback is crucial for understanding consumer satisfaction, guiding product development, and enhancing customer service strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While customer feedback is generally positive, it can also include negative critiques that are essential for improvement; thus, it should be approached with an open mind.

text: there's certain insights, data insights, research insights that were memified to the point where someone like Travis or Dara would just cite this insight in the middle of a meeting.
speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
context: Lenny asks about specific skills that have contributed most to Yuhki's career success. Yuhki emphasizes storytelling as crucial for product managers, explaining that good stories must drive action. He introduces the concept of 'memification' - making insights so memorable and sticky that executives naturally reference them in meetings.
text_ko: 어떤 인사이트들, 특히 데이터나 리서치 인사이트는 너무 밈화(memified)돼서 Travis나 Dara 같은 사람이 회의 중에 그냥 그걸 툭 꺼내 인용하곤 해요.
text_zh: 有些数据或研究方面的洞见，已经被玩成梗(memified)，到了像Travis或Dara在开会时会随口引用的地步。
text_es: Hay ciertos hallazgos de datos (data insights) y de investigación (research insights) que se han convertido en memes hasta el punto de que alguien como Travis o Dara los citaría en medio de una reunión.
key_sentence: certain insights, data insights, research insights that were memified to the point where someone like Travis or Dara would just cite this insight
original_text: I often talk about memification, which is this idea that I found this out most at Uber, I feel, where there's certain insights, data insights, research insights that were memmified to the point where someone like Travis or Dara would just cite this insight in the middle of a meeting, and you know that you've really done your job as, maybe, a researcher or a data scientist or product manager if people are able to do that and draw from that in that way.

vocabulary.definition: A deep understanding of a complex situation or problem, often derived from analysis of data or research.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, insights are crucial for making informed decisions, guiding strategy, and identifying opportunities for innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: While insights imply a level of understanding that goes beyond surface-level observations, they should be used judiciously to avoid overgeneralization.

vocabulary.definition: To refer to a source or authority as evidence for an argument or statement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In meetings and presentations, citing credible sources enhances the validity of claims and supports decision-making processes.
vocabulary.nuance: Citing should be done accurately and ethically to maintain credibility and avoid plagiarism.

text: There's something controversial about this idea that everyone can see what you're doing or that multiple designers can be in the file at the same time.
speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
context: Yuhki discusses advice for product-led growth founders about building emotional connection with users. He explains how Figma's controversial approach to collaborative design - allowing multiple designers in the same file simultaneously - created strong reactions that actually signaled they were driving meaningful change in how people work.
text_ko: 모두가 뭘 하고 있는지 다 볼 수 있다거나 여러 디자이너가 동시에 같은 파일(file)에 들어와 작업할 수 있다는 생각은 논란이 있어요.
text_zh: 关于“大家都能看到你在做什么”，或者“多人可以同时在同一个文件(file)里工作”这个观点，有争议。
text_es: Hay algo polémico en la idea de que todo el mundo pueda ver lo que haces o de que varios diseñadores puedan estar en el mismo archivo (file) al mismo tiempo.
key_sentence: There's something controversial about this idea that everyone can see what you're doing or that multiple designers can be in the file at the same time.
original_text: There's something controversial about this idea that everyone can see what you're doing or that multiple designers can be in the file at the same time. We like to say that one of the first responses we saw to Figma was, if this is the future of design, I'm quitting, right? I'm changing careers. And there's that tension of that narrative tension, but that is signal that you're part of this revolution and you're trying to change something.

vocabulary.definition: Causing or likely to cause public disagreement or controversy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, a controversial idea or product may provoke strong opinions, affecting stakeholder engagement and market reception.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'controversial' can indicate a healthy debate, it may also imply divisiveness, so it should be used carefully to avoid alienating audiences.

text: So Chris, our CTO, and I intervened. We created this new channel, private channel called Concerning Tweets, and it just, we're this small group of us that Dylan can drop us in. And these are tweets that aren't going viral, by any means.
speaker: Yuhki Yamashita
context: Yuhki continues describing Dylan Field's obsessive customer feedback monitoring. When Dylan's habit of sharing concerning tweets in team channels became disruptive, Yuhki and the CTO created a private 'Concerning Tweets' channel to contain the process while still capturing valuable signals from low-engagement customer feedback.
text_ko: 그래서 우리 CTO인 크리스랑 제가 개입했어요. 'Concerning Tweets'라는 비공개 채널(private channel)을 새로 만들었고, 딜런이 문제가 될 만한 트윗을 우리 소수의 팀에게 바로 올려줄 수 있게 했어요. 그리고 이런 트윗들은 결코 바이럴(viral)이 되는 건 아니에요.
text_zh: 于是我和我们的首席技术官（CTO）Chris出面了。我们新建了一个私密频道（private channel），叫“Concerning Tweets”，就是个小圈子，Dylan可以把推文丢到里面给我们看。那些推文根本没火，绝对谈不上走红（going viral）。
text_es: Así que Chris, nuestro director de tecnología (CTO), y yo intervenimos. Creamos un canal nuevo y privado llamado Tuits preocupantes (Concerning Tweets), y somos un grupo reducido al que Dylan puede enviar esos tuits. Y son tuits que ni de lejos se están volviendo virales.
key_sentence: we created this new channel, private channel called Concerning Tweets
original_text: So Chris, our CTO, and I intervened. We created this new channel, private channel called Concerning Tweets, and it just, we're this small group of us that Dylan can drop us in. And these are tweets that aren't going viral, by any means. They're just things that you see is with one like, sometimes zero likes, but he feels there's an essence of truth to them and we make sure that we look at what's going on there and see if there isn't something much bigger that we should be focusing on.

vocabulary.definition: A medium or pathway through which information, communication, or goods are transmitted.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a channel can refer to communication pathways, such as marketing channels or distribution channels, that facilitate the flow of information or products.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'channel' can imply a structured or formalized method of communication, so it is best used when discussing established pathways rather than informal interactions.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to content that spreads rapidly and widely, often through social media or online platforms.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and tech, 'viral' describes campaigns or content that achieve significant reach and engagement, often leading to increased brand visibility and customer acquisition.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'viral' is generally positive, suggesting popularity, it can also imply a lack of control over the message, so it should be used with an understanding of potential risks.
